content.value: Document Type - Lab Results. These documents are processed by athenahealth, for example, lab results obtained from a blood draw, fluid specimen, or a biopsy/surgical excision. Lab results are with the laboratory name, the date and time of the specimen collection, analytes and values, growth rate, or observations of tissue samples. Whenever possible, structured analytes should be entered on documents. Analytes are entered by practice users unless they are received via interface. This feature allows the user to retrieve, add or modify information of a specific patient or a specific lab result of a patient. It also provides a facility to retrieve lab results document in HTML. The document content could be images, XML.etc. The Lab Result Changed Subscription feature will allow the user to retrieve, delete, create or modify changes to lab results. The user will need to subscribe. For more information about subscriptions, please refer to

Obtained from a blood draw, fluid specimen, or a biopsy/surgical excision, lab results appear in the Results section of a patient’s chart. By default, lab result documents are created in an open status. However, creating lab results in a closed status is encouraged if the practice has already reviewed this data via another mechanism.
Whenever possible, structured analytes should be entered on documents, and clinicalordertype (test type) and clinicalprovider (performing lab/data source) should always be specified.
Note: Subclassification is not available for this document class.

API users can add and update lab analyte results through the existing lab result document POST and PUT endpoints for a specified patient. An analyte is a lab result value, such as glucose, HDL cholesterol, and WBC.

The user's application must be the primary source of the lab analytes added through the lab result API. The analytes being uploaded into athenaOne are only a copy of the data available through the user's own application. The user is responsible for contacting/warning a patient’s provider or care team if any analyte result collected from a patient is outside of a reasonable threshold.

Using the lab result document endpoint, users can create a lab result document with one or more lab analytes. The lab analyte value in the POST API is a url-encoded JSON structure. Each entry contains items related to an analyte. Example lab analyte value for the POST:

fields.title: Document Type - Lab Result Adding Lab Analytes Code Sample

content.value: The analytename is required in order to POST a lab analyte. All other fields are optional.

Lab analytes associated with lab result documents can be updated through the lab result PUT endpoint. You must first get the labresultid of the lab result. You can get this from the lab result GET API via:

After retrieving the labresultid, you will must then get the analyteid of the analyte that you want to update. The analyteid uniquely identifies that particular analyte result. You can use the analyteid to update the fields associated with that particular analyte result using the document specific lab result GET API via:

fields.title: Document Type - Lab Result Updating Lab Analytes Sample API Response

content.value: Once you have the analyteid(s), you will must add a ‘“analyteid” : “{analyteid}}’ line to all the entries of the analyte(s) you are updating.
If an entry doesn’t have an analyteid, it will be considered a new analyte instead of an update and added to the lab result document.
Example lab analyte value for the PUT:

content.value: NOTE: The above example would update the HGB A1C analyte since the analyteid was provided and add the ACTH, Plasma analyte to the lab result since the analyteid was NOT provided.

lastmodifieduser.description: The user who last modified this document.

originalfilename.description: The original file name of this document.

performinglabaddress1.description: This is the address1 field of the performing lab. For point-of-care tests this is the department. Otherwise, it is the clinical provider

performinglabaddress2.description: This is the address2 field of the performing lab. For point-of-care tests this is the department. Otherwise, it is the clinical provider

performinglabcity.description: This is the city of the performing lab. For point-of-care tests this is the department. Otherwise, it is the clinical provider

performinglabname.description: This is the name of the performing lab. For point-of-care tests this is the department. Otherwise, it is the clinical provider

performinglabstate.description: This is the state of the performing lab. For point-of-care tests this is the department. Otherwise, it is the clinical provider

performinglabzip.description: This is the zip code of the performing lab. For point-of-care tests this is the department. Otherwise, it is the clinical provider

portalpublisheddatetime.description: The date the document was published to the portal in format (yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss).

priority.description: Document priority, when available. 1 is high, 2 is normal. Some labs use other numbers or characters that are lab-specific.

receivedfacilityordercode.description: The code as received from the facility via HL7 in OBR.4.

description.description: The description of the code received in OBR.4.2.

code.description: Order identifier for the result codified data.

display.description: Order text for the result codified data.

system.description: Order coding system for the result codified data.

orderloinc.description: Laboratory code that identifies the result codified data.

tietoorderid.description: Order ID of the order this document is tied to, if any

subscriptionEndpoints.endpointTitle: Unsubscribe to all/specific change events for lab events
subscriptionEndpoints.endpointDescription: Deletes a specific event which is no longer required

inputParameters.name: eventname
inputParameters.description: By default, you are unsubscribed from all possible events.  If you only wish to unsubscribe from an individual event, pass the event name with this argument.

success.description: Returns if the call to manipulate subscriptions for labresults was successful.
